title: Preparing sequencing grade RNAs from a small number of FACS-sorted larvae macrophages isolated from enzyme free dissociated zebrafish larvae
author: Begon-Pescia, Boireau, et al.
materials: For 1L: 1.5 ml of Instant Ocean Sea Salt mixture stock solution (40 g/L), 40 µl 10 N NaOH and 300 µl methylene blue stock solution (sigma # M9140)-Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH MW=40.

-1X Dulbecco's Phosphate-Buffered Saline (1X DPBS), no calcium, no magnesium (Life Technologies # 14190094)-Ultrapure 0.5 M EDTA, pH 8.0 (Invitrogen™ # 15575–020)-Fetal Bovine Serum, qualified, heat inactivated (FBSi Gibco™ # 10500064)-Working buffer (at 4 °C): 500 ml 0.9X DPBS with 2% FBSi and 2 mM EDTA

8.To minimize RNA degradation and loss of material, the mCherry-F positive and mCherry-F negative sorted cells (from amputated (cut) and non-amputated (uncut) Tg(mfap4:mCherry-F) larvae) were separately collected directly into 100 µl RLT/β-ME Qiagen's lysis buffer into RNase/DNase-free 1.5 ml microfuge tubes.9.After sorting, correctly close the cap of the collecting tube and vortex vigorously (2 × 5 s). Put the tube quickly on ice to process total RNA extraction immediately with RNeasy micro kit. Alternatively, tubes can be stored at - 80 °C for a long-term storage, until extraction of total RNA with RNeasy micro kit.

Reagents
-Qiagen RNeasy micro Kit (Cat. No. # 74004)-Ultrapure DNase/RNase-free distilled water (Invitrogen # 10977035)-70% ethanol (Ethanol Absolute # 20821.310 and DNase/RNase-free water)

Procedure
1.After cell sorting, or thawing from −80 °C, lysates are kept on ice.2.Vortex vigorously and with a pipet with sterile tip, measure precisely the exact final volume of sorted cells mixed with the RLT/βME Qiagen's Buffer.3.According to the manufacturer's instructions, add exactly the same volume of 70% ethanol to the final volume of sorted sample, and mix immediately. As an example, 57,000 mCherry-F positive macrophages sorted into 100 µl RLT/βME Qiagen's buffer lead to a final volume of 200 µl; the total volume of 70% ethanol that needs to be added is therefore 200 µl.4.Follow the Qiagen RNeasy micro Kit procedure according to the manufacturer's instructions.5.Spare 1.5 µl of each RNA sample into a new RNase/DNase-free 0.5 ml microfuge tubes that will be used for the qualitative assessment of total RNA using the Bioanalyzer 2100.6.Keep the rest of RNA samples at −20 °C for a short-term storage or at −80 °C for a long-term storage.

steps.title: Amputate caudal fin folds
steps.instruction: Anaesthetize 360 Tg(mfap4:mCherry‑F) larvae (and 200 wild‑type AB larvae) in zebrafish water containing 0.016 % tricaine (stock 4 mg ml⁻¹; add 400 µl stock to 25 ml water for 60 larvae). After ~10 min, place the dish under a stereomicroscope, hold each larva laterally with a brush or thin tip, and cut the tip of the caudal fin fold just posterior to the notochord using a sterile size‑10 carbon‑steel scalpel blade without damaging the notochord. Transfer the amputated larvae with a transfer pipet to a fresh petri dish containing tricaine‑free zebrafish water and let them recover at 28 °C until the desired post‑amputation time point. Use the following reagents: tricaine stock (400 mg in 100 ml water, buffered with 2.1 ml 1 M Tris pH 9, stored –20 °C), zebrafish water (1.5 ml Instant Ocean per L, 40 µl 10 N NaOH, 300 µl methylene blue), and 10 N NaOH stock (40 g in 50 ml H₂O, bring to 100 ml, store RT).

steps.title: Enzyme‑free dissociation for FACS
steps.instruction: Keep all reagents and cell suspensions on ice (4 °C) and process no more than 150 whole larvae per 70‑µm cell strainer. Prepare a cold working buffer (500 ml 0.9X DPBS with 2 % heat‑inactivated FBS and 2 mM EDTA). For each batch, place a 70‑µm mesh strainer on a 50 ml Falcon tube, transfer up to 120 anaesthetized larvae (from two petri dishes) onto the strainer with a 25 ml pipet, crush the larvae with a 2.5 ml syringe plunger, and rinse the filter with 30–50 ml cold working buffer. Repeat for all larvae (e.g., three tubes for 360 larvae). Centrifuge each tube at 1700 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C, keep the tube on ice, and discard the supernatant by inverting. Resuspend each pellet in 1 ml cold working buffer with a P1000 pipet, then bring the volume up to 10 ml with additional cold buffer. Filter the 10 ml suspension through a 40‑µm mesh placed on a new 50 ml Falcon tube, rinsing the filter with 2–6 ml cold buffer. Pool filtrates from the same experimental condition, centrifuge again at 1700 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C, keep on ice, discard supernatant, resuspend the final pellet in 1.5 ml cold working buffer, and transfer to a 5 ml round‑bottom polystyrene FACS tube. Keep samples on ice and proceed to sorting promptly.

steps.title: Sort mCherry‑F positive/negative cells
steps.instruction: Add SYTOX™ Red Dead Cell Stain to the wild‑type (unlabeled) cell suspension at a final concentration of 5 nM (add 1 µl of 5 µM stock to 1 ml suspension). For the Tg(mfap4:mCherry‑F) suspension, keep cells on ice and sort using a BD FACSAria™ IIu equipped with a 70 µm nozzle, 87 kHz frequency, 70 psi sheath pressure, and sheath fluid of 1X DPBS (no calcium). Excite mCherry‑F with a 488 nm laser (100 mW) and collect emission with 600 LP then 610/20 nm band‑pass filters; excite SYTOX™ Red with a 633 nm laser (30 mW) and collect with a 660/20 nm filter. Maintain the sample chamber at 4 °C, agitate at 300 rpm, and set the flow rate to 3–5 µl min⁻¹ to acquire 5000–6000 events s⁻¹ with a sort efficiency of 90–100 %. Collect the sorted mCherry‑F positive and negative populations directly into 100 µl RLT/β‑ME lysis buffer (Qiagen RNeasy micro kit) in RNase/DNase‑free 1.5 ml microfuge tubes, vortex vigorously twice for 5 s each, and place the tubes on ice. If sorting exceeds 30 min, change the collection tube or filter the suspension through a 40‑µm mesh to prevent nozzle clogging. Store tubes at –80 °C if RNA extraction will be delayed.

steps.title: Extract total RNA from sorted cells
steps.instruction: Keep lysates on ice after sorting (or after thawing from –80 °C). Vortex vigorously, then measure the exact total volume of cell suspension mixed with RLT/β‑ME buffer. Add an equal volume of 70 % ethanol to the mixture (e.g., 100 µl RLT/β‑ME + 100 µl ethanol = 200 µl total for 57 000 cells). Process the sample with the Qiagen RNeasy Micro Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol, including on‑column DNase I treatment. Elute RNA with 14 µl RNase‑free water into RNase/DNase‑free 1.5 ml microfuge tubes. Immediately set aside 1.5 µl of each eluate in a RNase/DNase‑free 0.5 ml tube for qualitative assessment, keep the remaining RNA at –20 °C for short‑term storage or at –80 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Assess RNA quality with Bioanalyzer
steps.instruction: Thaw the 1.5 µl RNA aliquots on ice. Using the Agilent RNA 6000 Pico Kit (Agilent #5067‑1513) and the 2100 Bioanalyzer instrument (Agilent #G2939BA) with its chip‑priming station and vortex mixer, follow the kit’s manufacturer instructions to evaluate RNA concentration and integrity (RIN). Use a Qubit Fluorometer with the RNA HS Assay Kit for concentration if needed.
